items.title: Oil prices climb as U.S.-Iran tensions mount after Geneva talks

featured_image.name: Brent edges lower as traders turn focus to key U.S.-Iran talks

items.description:
Oil prices climbed on Wednesday as traders weighed rising U.S.-Iran tensions against cautious optimism following a second round of nuclear talks in Geneva, while global stock markets advanced in thin trading.

Brent crude rose more than 2% to around $69 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate also gained ground, as markets priced in geopolitical risk surrounding the Strait of Hormuz and the broader Middle East standoff.[1][2][3]

items.title: Nvidia sells off Arm stake as Meta deal lifts chip stocks

featured_image.name: Nvidia Sells Off Stake in Arm, a Company It Once Tried to Buy

items.description:
Nvidia disclosed it has sold its remaining stake in Arm, closing the loop on a once-ambitious effort to buy the chip designer, as investors focused instead on a newly expanded infrastructure partnership with Meta Platforms that helped buoy US stocks on Wednesday.

Broader markets opened higher with technology shares leading, after the Meta-Nvidia announcement eased jitters about a pullback in big-tech spending on artificial intelligence hardware.[1][2][3]

items.title: Ukraine-Russia peace talks end abruptly after two hours in Geneva
items.description:
US-mediated peace talks between Ukraine and Russia ended abruptly in Geneva on Wednesday after just two hours of negotiations, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accusing Moscow of deliberately prolonging the dialogue and criticizing US President Donald Trump for unfairly pressuring Kyiv rather than Russia to make concessions.

The second day of trilateral discussions concluded far more quickly than Tuesday's six-hour session, with neither side signaling any breakthrough on the nearly four-year conflict that has killed or wounded nearly two million people. Russian chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky described the talks as "difficult but businesslike," while Ukrainian officials confirmed the meeting lasted only around two hours.[1][2][3]

items.title: Astronomers find 'missing link' galaxies from early universe

featured_image.name: Astronomers Discover A Dusty Primordial Star Forming Galaxy

items.description: An international team of 48 astronomers from 14 countries, led by the University of Massachusetts Amherst, has identified a population of dusty, star-forming galaxies at the far edges of the universe that formed approximately one billion years after the Big Bang. The discovery, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, may represent a "missing link" in the timeline of galaxy evolution.[1][2][3]

items.title: European stocks hit record high as US-Iran talks show progress

featured_image.name: Iran foreign minister says progress made in nuclear talks ...

items.description:
Global equities advanced on Wednesday as investors welcomed signs of diplomatic progress between the United States and Iran following their second round of nuclear negotiations in Geneva, while oil prices hovered near two-week lows on hopes that a potential deal could ease supply disruption risks.

The STOXX 600 rose 0.8% to a record high of 626.36, led by gains in defense and banking stocks. Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 1.02% to close at 57,143.84, snapping a four-day losing streak. Several major Asian markets, including China, Hong Kong, South Korea, and Taiwan, remained closed for Lunar New Year holidays.[1][2][3]

items.title: New Zealand startup achieves world-first levitated magnet plasma confinement

featured_image.name: Half-ton magnet aces world-first 1.8 million°F fusion plasma ...

items.description:
A Wellington-based startup achieved what it describes as a world-first in nuclear fusion technology this week, demonstrating plasma confinement using a fully levitated superconducting magnet. The milestone drew New Zealand's Prime Minister to witness the event firsthand, as the small South Pacific nation positions itself as an unexpected player in the global race for clean energy.

OpenStar Technologies publicly showcased its "Junior" prototype on February 16, successfully confining plasma while a 560-kilogram superconducting magnet hovered inside a vacuum chamber without mechanical support or external power connections. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon attended alongside Ministers Shane Jones and Christopher Bishop, with Luxon himself initiating plasmas in the device.[1][2][3]

items.title: Bayer shares drop as Roundup settlement optimism fades

featured_image.name: European shares run out of steam by close as Bayer, energy ...

items.description:
Bayer has agreed to a proposed $7.25 billion settlement to resolve tens of thousands of U.S. lawsuits alleging its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer, the German pharmaceutical and agricultural giant announced on Tuesday. The deal, if approved, would cover both current and future claims tied to non-Hodgkin lymphoma, but shares fell sharply on Wednesday as investors weighed the massive financial burden against lingering legal uncertainty.

The settlement, filed in St. Louis Circuit Court in Missouri, would establish a long-term claims program funded by capped annual payments over up to 21 years, with the majority of funds distributed in the first five years. Bayer said its litigation provisions and liabilities would rise from €7.8 billion to €11.8 billion, and the company now expects negative free cash flow for 2026.[1][2][3]

items.title: Blackstone, EQT and CVC bid for Volkswagen's Everllence unit

featured_image.name: Everllence launches investor process for Deggendorf site

items.description:
Volkswagen has attracted first-round offers from three of the world's largest private equity firms for its heavy-engine division Everllence in a sale that could value the unit between €5 billion and €6 billion, The Financial Times reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.[1][2][3]

Blackstone, Sweden's EQT, and CVC Capital Partners have submitted bids for the division, which manufactures shipping engines and heat pumps, following a deadline for initial offers that passed on February 12. The German automaker is planning to sell a majority stake while retaining a minority holding in the business.[4][3][5]
